doc.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Advice for singers: breathing and listening
summary: Breathe deep, learn from Sinatra, Dean Martin and others, tell a story as in the Ben Webster tale.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Hat size. I’ve got to borrow that one too. That’s great. So I know you have to get on the road. Do you have a piece of advice for aspiring singers? What should they always have?

Lots of air. Breathe deep. Don’t interrupt yourself when you sing. [sings] She gets too hungry for dinner [exaggerated breath] at eight. Don’t do that. Listen to Frank [Sinatra]. Nobody breathes better than that you know. I mean I’m a big fan of Dean Martin.

You want to learn how to sing, as far as like being relaxed and not take yourself too serious, watch Dean Martin. He’s having a great time, he sings in tune, he sings in time, he’s not drunk. You know. I mean I like a lot of singers. Anita O’Day. I listen to a lot of female singers. Anita O’Day, she’s fantastic. Carmen [McRae] I mean everybody knows Carmen, Sarah [Vaughan], Ella [Fitzgerald]. You know, Billie [Holiday]. Anita O’Day. I don’t sing like Chet Baker, I don’t sing like Jimmy Scott, but I sure can listen to them. So listen to all the greats. Listen to all the horn players who play songs.
Yeah, you said that, I know you said that, “some of my biggest influences are sax players.”

Yeah. You know let me reiterate another story. I mean these are stories that we probably know. The Ben Webster story where he’s doing a record of ballads. And he’s one take right after the other. One take, that’s a take, okay next. Next take. They get to like the fifth tune and they’re playing and Ben just stops. So everybody stops and the engineer says, “Ben, is there a problem?” He says, “yeah, man, I forgot the words.” He’s playing a tenor. “Yeah but I forgot the words.” So it’s important to tell a story and to be connected to the story. If you can’t connect, sing something that you can connect to. I mean I’ll probably never record “I Feel Pretty.”
All right. I won’t expect that from you. Maybe you could describe someone else who’s feeling pretty and put that spin on it. © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
